title: Exact cohomology ladder for the internal-Hom filtered-colimit comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe, with $\mathcal O$ commutative [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix the functorial K-injective target models for $H(A,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,N)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models]. For any small filtered diagram $N:I\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], put $N_\infty=\varinjlim_iN_i$ termwise and let $\alpha_A:\varinjlim_iH(A,N_i)\to H(A,N_\infty)$ be the image in $D(\mathcal M)$ of the canonical complex cocone map on these models. All colimits here are termwise sheaf colimits. For every small filtered complex diagram $(K_i)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, there is a natural isomorphism
$$H^q(\varinjlim_iK_i)\cong\varinjlim_iH^q(K_i).$$
Consequently termwise filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms and common cohomological lower bounds. Let $A\xrightarrow u B\xrightarrow v C\xrightarrow w A[1]$ be any distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the sequences
$$\cdots\to\varinjlim_iH^{q-1}(H(A,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(C,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(B,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^q(H(A,N_i))\to\varinjlim_iH^{q+1}(H(C,N_i))\to\cdots$$
and
$$\cdots\to H^{q-1}(H(A,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(C,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(B,N_\infty))\to H^q(H(A,N_\infty))\to H^{q+1}(H(C,N_\infty))\to\cdots$$
are exact, and form a commuting ladder whose vertical arrows at $X=A,B,C$ are $H^q(\alpha_X)$ under the displayed cohomology-colimit identification. The arrows in both rows are those induced by precomposition with $u,v,w$; for $w$ one uses the signed source-shift comparison $H(A[1],N)\cong H(A,N)[-1]$ (cochain convention $K[n]^q=K^{q+n}$, $d_{K[n]}=(-1)^nd_K$), which on the Hom-complex models reindexes components and multiplies degree-$q$ components by $(-1)^q$, independently of $N$. Commutativity includes every connecting square, with these specified signs. No boundedness, continuity or constructibility assumption is imposed on $A,B,C$ or $N$.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), old proof steps 1 and 4: exact termwise colimits, cycles and boundaries, and the natural long exact comparison including connecting maps; Modules on Sites Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); Derived Categories Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological).

proof.text: Work throughout in the fixed universe. The category $\mathcal M$ has all the required small colimits and exact filtered colimits by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. For a complex diagram $K$ its termwise colimit is a complex: the induced differentials have square zero because their composites with every colimit leg do. A cocone of complexes factors uniquely degreewise, and these degreewise factorizations commute with the differentials by the same cocone equations. Thus the termwise construction is indeed the colimit complex. This uses smallness of the site and of $I$, but no boundedness.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits): exact filtered colimits of module sheaves

proof.text: Write $Z_i^q=\ker(d_i^q)$ and $B_i^q=\operatorname{im}(d_i^{q-1})$. These form diagrams since the transition chain maps commute with $d$. Apply the exact colimit functor of [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] to $0\to Z_i^q\to K_i^q\to B_i^{q+1}\to0$ and to the monomorphisms $B_i^{q+1}\to K_i^{q+1}$. The resulting factorization of $d_\infty^q$ identifies its kernel with $\varinjlim Z_i^q$ and its image with $\varinjlim B_i^{q+1}$. Now apply that same exact functor to $0\to B_i^q\to Z_i^q\to H^q(K_i)\to0$. The quotient of the identified cycles by the identified boundaries is $\varinjlim H^q(K_i)$, proving the asserted isomorphism by the definition of cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Denote its inverse by $\theta_K^q:\varinjlim H^q(K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(K_\infty)$. Every identification was induced by the kernel inclusion or the quotient map, so it commutes with maps of diagrams and satisfies $\theta_K^q\circ\iota_i=H^q(K_i\to K_\infty)$.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), applied to cycles and boundaries

proof.text: For an objectwise quasi-isomorphism $K_i\to L_i$, the maps $H^q(K_i)\to H^q(L_i)$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Their inverses form a natural transformation, so their colimit is an isomorphism. Step 2 then shows that $K_\infty\to L_\infty$ is a quasi-isomorphism. If all $H^q(K_i)$ vanish for $q<a$, step 2 gives $H^q(K_\infty)=\varinjlim 0=0$ for $q<a$. The bound $a$ must be common to the diagram; no bound was used to construct $\theta$.

Put $J_i=I(N_i)$, $J_\infty=I(N_\infty)$, and $t_i=I(N_i\to N_\infty)$, using the fixed replacement functor [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a source complex $P$, set $F(P)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J_i)$ and $G(P)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J_\infty)$. Postcomposition by $t_i$ induces the chain map $a_P:F(P)\to G(P)$. For any source chain map $f:P\to P'$, pre- and postcomposition commute componentwise [def-pur-hom-complex], hence $a_P F(f)=G(f)a_{P'}$. A source quasi-isomorphism induces quasi-isomorphisms of all these Hom complexes by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined-universes], applied with the identity on each K-injective target. Step 3 makes $F(f)$ a quasi-isomorphism as well. Consequently $QF,QG$ and $Qa$ descend to the source derived category by its localization property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality for an inverted quasi-isomorphism follows by multiplying the chain-map naturality equality by its two inverses; hence the equality holds for every derived source morphism. The descended component $Qa_P$ is precisely $\alpha_P$ from the statement, with no assertion that the colimit of K-injectives is K-injective.

source.place: Tags 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined) and 08J7 (section-internal-hom); naturality of the fixed target cocone

proof.text: For a target complex $J$, define $s_{P,J}:\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[1],J)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,J)[-1]$ by $(s^n f)^p=(-1)^n f^{p-1}$. This is an invertible product reindexing. Substituting $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$ into the Hom differential [def-pur-hom-complex] gives, on both sides of $s^{n+1}d=d s^n$, the component $(-1)^{n+1}d_J f^{p-1}-f^p d_P^p$. Thus it is a chain isomorphism with exactly the stipulated sign. For a target chain map $t:J\to J'$, both $s_{P,J'}\mathcal Hom(P[1],t)$ and $\mathcal Hom(P,t)[-1]s_{P,J}$ send $f$ in degree $n$ to $((-1)^n t f^{p-1})_p$. The same identity holds after taking the termwise colimit: shifts merely relabel degrees and multiply differentials by $-1$, so commute with this colimit. In particular $s_\infty a_{P[1]}=a_P[-1](\varinjlim_i s_i)$. These equalities also descend through inverted source quasi-isomorphisms as in step 4. This proves the required source-shift compatibility of $\alpha$, without commuting any infinite product with a colimit.

source.place: Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), explicit signed source shift for Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated)

proof.text: For each target $N_i$, and for $N_\infty$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] sends the given distinguished triangle contravariantly to a distinguished triangle of derived internal Homs, with the signed shift identification. Applying [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the second displayed row and the corresponding row before colimiting for each $i$. More explicitly, the arrow preceding $H^q(H(C,N))$ is the composite $H^{q-1}(H(A,N))\cong H^q(H(A[1],N))\xrightarrow{H^q(H(w,N))}H^q(H(C,N))$, where the first isomorphism is induced by the inverse of $s$ from step 5. The arrows at $C,B,A$ are precomposition by $v,u,w$, respectively, with the same formula translated in degree for $w$. This realizes the arrows prescribed in the statement. A rotation convention that negates a boundary negates it for every target; multiplication by $-1$ does not change its image or kernel, so exactness holds with the stated normalization in every integer degree.

For each $i$, write $r_{X,i}=H(X,N_i\to N_\infty)$. The precomposition equalities of step 4 for $u,v,w$ give $r_{B,i}H(v,N_i)=H(v,N_\infty)r_{C,i}$ and $r_{A,i}H(u,N_i)=H(u,N_\infty)r_{B,i}$, and also $r_{C,i}H(w,N_i)=H(w,N_\infty)r_{A[1],i}$. By step 5, $s_\infty r_{A[1],i}=r_{A,i}[-1]s_i$. Composing the latter two equalities with $s_i^{-1}$ gives the connecting square after the identification $H^q(H(A[1],N))=H^{q-1}(H(A,N))$. These are morphisms of the reversed Hom triangles; equivalently their cohomology ladders are the morphisms of long exact sequences in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder]. This verifies the connecting square by its actual precomposition and shift maps. The same argument for a transition $N_i\to N_j$ makes the rows into an $I$-diagram of exact sequences. All equalities hold for the derived $w$, by the localization argument of step 4.

Take the colimit of the exact rows of step 7. Exactness of filtered colimits [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] gives the first displayed row: at each spot, factor the preceding arrow through its image and apply exactness to $0\to\operatorname{im}(d_{k-1})\to E_k\to\operatorname{im}(d_k)\to0$. The resulting kernel equals the preceding image, just as in step 2. For $K_i=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(X,J_i)$, naturality of $\theta$ from step 2 shows that $c_X^q=H^q(\alpha_X)\circ\theta_K^q$ has $c_X^q\circ\iota_i=H^q(r_{X,i})$. Thus the universal colimit maps of the stagewise ladders are exactly the asserted vertical arrows under the cohomology-colimit identification. For each horizontal arrow, composing its proposed square with every $\iota_i$ gives the commuting square of step 7, including its specified signed connecting square. The universal property of the colimit makes the two composites equal. Varying $q$ proves every square and every exact spot of the infinite ladder. Only finite exact sequences were colimited at each spot; there is no boundedness or continuity hypothesis.

No new nodes; 8 steps, each under 2000 characters. Sources are Stacks only: 08JC (sites-cohomology l.8948), 03DB (sites-modules l.1358), 05RS (derived l.3618); all checked, no SGA. Steps 1–3: exactness of filtered colimits from lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian (same hypotheses) gives the colimit complex, ker d_∞ = colim Z and im d_∞ = colim B, so H^q(colim) = colim H^q, naturally, with θ∘ι_i = H^q(leg). Quasi-isomorphisms and common lower bounds are preserved. Step 4: source quasi-isomorphism invariance of the internal Hom complexes into K-injective targets comes from lem-pur-rhom-well-defined-universes with s = id, then step 3 for the colimit, so F, G and a descend through the localisation; no colimit of K-injectives is used. Step 5: I rechecked by hand the sign of s, (s^n f)^p = (−1)^n f^{p−1}, against the def-pur-hom-complex differential and d_{K[−1]} = −d_K; both sides give (−1)^{n+1} d_J f^{p−1} − f^p d_P^p, and s commutes with postcomposition and with termwise colimits. Step 6: rows exact by lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction plus the long exact sequence. The triangle lemma does not specify its shift isomorphism, but changing the connecting arrow by any isomorphism of its source leaves kernel and image unchanged, so exactness holds with the s-normalised boundary (advisory: the worker only argued the ±1 case). Steps 7–8: stagewise squares are checked directly, the filtered colimit of exact rows is exact, c_X∘ι_i = H^q(r_{X,i}), and testing each square on the legs gives commutativity, including the connecting square. Edge cases checked: one-object site, constant diagram, terminal-object index, split triangle with w = 0, and K_i = (R→R, ·i) over divisibility.
